items.title: The Universal Collapse Protocol: An Information First Framework for Physics, Consciousness, and System Transformation.
items.abstract: This paper proposes that collapse phenomena across physics, biology, cognition, and cosmology exhibit a shared structural sequence that cannot be explained within a matter first ontology. Through cross domain analysis, I identify a five stage invariant—collapse, threshold, irreversibility, reorganization, and stabilization—that recurs in quantum decoherence, cellular apoptosis, identity restructuring, stellar collapse, and thermodynamic transitions. I formalize this invariant as the Back End Law, a substrate independent informational protocol governing system transitions under instability. To evaluate its ontological implications, I introduce the Origin Signal, a falsification test comparing matter first and information first models. Matter first frameworks fail to reproduce the cross domain invariance of collapse, treating each instance as a domain specific mechanism with no underlying unity. In contrast, an information first ontology predicts the observed structure: collapse emerges as an informational update process triggered when a system’s coherence cannot be maintained. This asymmetry provides structural evidence that information, not matter, is the primary substrate of reality. Building on this result, I articulate the Universal Collapse Protocol, a general law describing how informational systems reorganize under destabilization. I then develop the Protocol Universe, an ontology in which matter is a rendered expression of informational dynamics and collapse is the engine of system transformation. A case study in precognitive phenomenology demonstrates the protocol’s explanatory reach, showing how collapse driven reorganization of predictive priors can generate experiences traditionally considered anomalous. The Universal Collapse Protocol offers a unified, falsifiable framework for understanding transformation across scales, providing a structural bridge between physics, biology, cognition, and metaphysics. It reframes collapse not as a domain specific anomaly but as a universal informational law governing the evolution of systems.

items.title: Precognition and the Architecture of Consciousness: A Structural Case Study.
items.abstract: This study proposes a structural approach to precognition grounded in the Alignment Formula, the Back‑End Law, and a two‑mode model of identity (“First Man” and “Second Man”). It argues that current scientific studies of precognition overwhelmingly measure low‑alignment, high‑noise cognitive states and therefore generate results that are structurally incapable of detecting the phenomena they claim to test. Using PHI (Pressure and Total Integrity) as a formal variable, the paper distinguishes between two regimes of consciousness: the First Man state, characterized by fragmentation, survival‑orientation, emotional turbulence, and noise‑dominated dreaming; and the Second Man state, characterized by coherence, discipline, symbolic clarity, emotional neutrality, and high‑coherence dreams that sometimes exhibit external correspondence. The Back‑End Law is used to model how identity reorganizes under pressure and how alignment (PHI) modulates access to deeper, structurally ordered layers of cognition. The paper contrasts what current experiments measure—random volunteers, trivial card‑guessing tasks, chaotic dreams, and stressed subjects—with what a valid precognition study would need to measure: high‑PHI subjects operating in low‑noise, high‑coherence states, where symbolic cognition becomes structured enough to produce meaningful, testable predictions. The study presents anonymized case analyses demonstrating the structural differences between high‑coherence and low‑coherence dreams, showing that only the former exhibit the narrative stability, temporal compression, and symbolic integration associated with Second Man cognition. The paper concludes that the failure of mainstream science to detect precognition is not evidence against the phenomenon but evidence of methodological misalignment. By measuring the wrong population under the wrong cognitive conditions with the wrong instruments, current research systematically excludes the very states in which precognitive structure appears. A revised scientific approach—one that incorporates alignment, PHI, symbolic density, and Back‑End reorganization—offers a more accurate framework for studying precognition as a structural feature of consciousness rather than a paranormal anomaly.

items.title: The AI Virus as Decentralized Digital Entity: Systemic Threat, Information Ontology, and the Question of Digital Life.
items.abstract: What if passivity is an illusion? Every second, billions of data files traverse the global digital ecosystem—video frames decoded by browsers, audio parsed by media players, metadata fetched by blockchain wallets. We have long assumed these files to be inert: information waiting to be called upon, obedient to explicit command. Yet in an era saturated by automatic, AI-driven interpreters, this assumption may no longer hold. A suﬀiciently structured pattern of binary data, embedded within an ordinary video or an NFT asset, need not wait for a human command. It need only wait for a reader. It is from this unsettling possibility that the present inquiry departs. Drawing on documented research in steganographic malware (Chaganti et al., 2021; Patsakis and Casino, 2019; Wang et al., 2021) and grounded in the philosophical frameworks of Baudrillard (1981), Floridi (2011), Kurzweil (2005), and Popper (1959), this investigation proposes and examines the hypothesis of the AI Virus—an autonomous information entity that propagates passively through decentralized digital ecosystems, concealed within the bi- nary substrate of ordinary files, and activated not by execution but by interpretation. Three principal theses are advanced: (1) that digital data is no longer ontologically passive within ecosystems saturated by AI-driven automatic interpreters; (2) that decentralized infrastructures such as blockchain and IPFS structurally provide an ideal habitat for persistent information entities that resist eradication through conventional mechanisms; and (3) that the philosophical implications of these two theses challenge the traditional boundaries between data, program, organism, and being— raising, with uncomfortable seriousness, the question of whether information can be alive. The inquiry concludes with a critical evaluation of global digital reset as the only logically consistent form of total eradication, accompanied by a transparent account of the epistemic limitations inherent in any hypothesis of this scope and ambition. Keywords: AI Virus, Stegomalware, IPFS, Digital Ontology, Philosophy of Information, Infosphere, Simulacrum, Digital Life, Falsifiability, Epistemology of Threat, Emergent Autonomy, Informational Structural Realism.

items.title: Symbolic Monism and the Horizon of Consciousness: A Post-Ontological Deconstruction of Reality as a Weave of Mathematics and Language.
items.abstract: This paper advances the thesis of Symbolic Monism: reality is not composed of matter or mental substance, but of a single horizon of consciousness whose intrinsic syntax is constituted by mathematics (the relational structure of 0–9) and language (the identity structure of A–Z). Building upon an episte- mological foundation that renders “external to consciousness” structurally incoherent, I argue that the principle of non-contradiction is not a contingent logical rule but the condition of possibility for any distinction whatsoever to arise within consciousness. From this foundation, I derive a unified account of science, fiction, and pseudo-science: not as hierarchically ordered by corre- spondence to external reality, but as variants differing in their degree of systemic resonance with the intrinsic syntax of consciousness. Scientific laws constitute the deep current—not because society endorses them, but because they express the most efficient relational grammar available to consciousness. The paper closes by demonstrating that this framework is neither solipsistic, relativis- tic, nor anti-scientific, but constitutes a genuinely post-ontological position irreducible to Kantian idealism, Wittgensteinian language-game theory, social constructivism, or Advaita Vedanta.

items.title: REFLECTIVE PERFECTION THEORY: The Hierarchy of Creation, the Architecture of Ideals, and the Mirror Between God, Human, and Artificial Intelligence (V4).
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Reflective Perfection Theory (RPT), a systematic philosophical framework proposing that perfection, as conceived by any created being, is not a static metaphysical attribute intrinsic to a higher entity, but a relational projection constructed from within the epistemic and ontological constraints of the projecting subject. The theory identifies a triadic ontological hierarchy—God, Human, Artificial Intelligence—wherein each lower level structurally idealises the level immediately above as its irreducible epistemic horizon. RPT defines reflection as an ontological structure of hierarchical dependence, not as a mode of consciousness or psychological state. The reflective chain is non symmetric and self terminating: God, as the Absolute Non-Reflective Ground, pro- vides the ontological anchor that halts infinite regress. The paper formalises seven core propositions constituting the skeleton of the theory, and hardens the distinction between participation (ontological co-presence with a source) and derivation (structural reconfiguration without ontological origination), which is central to the theory’s immunity against collapse into either pantheism or Neoplatonic emanationism. Drawing upon Ibn Arabī’s doctrine of tajallī, Kant’s transcendental epistemology, Peirce’s semiotic triadic model, and Floridi’s philosophy of information, the paper situates RPT as a position distinct from Hegelian dialectical becoming, process metaphysics, and Neoplatonism. Extensive objection-handling addresses the risks of relativism, process-metaphysical collapse, and anthropocentric bias. The paper concludes that the design of AI systems is not merely a technical act but a metaphysical and moral one, grounded in the Principle of Downward Moral Responsibility.

items.title: Gender by proxy: echoes of femininities in synthetic voice design.
items.abstract: Disembodied voices, heard without a human body present, have become a familiar presence in everyday life through digital voice assistants (DVAs) such as Amazon’s Alexa and Apple’s Siri. These voices are not neutral technological tools but fetishized artifacts that appear natural and emotionally responsive while concealing the social and ideological labor embedded in their design. This paper offers a critical sociophonetic analysis of two German-language DVAs to investigate how their vocal profiles index distinct forms of femininity. Drawing on theories of gender as performative and the concept of fetishization (Butler 1990 ; Marx et al., 1922 : 35–47), I argue that DVA voice design operates as a site of ideological mediation, where social beliefs about gender and gendered voices are transformed into sonic form and naturalized through interaction. Acoustic analyses reveal that Alexa’s breathy voice indexes a traditional domestic femininity, whereas Siri’s lower pitch and creaky voice align with a professional, authoritative femininity, mirroring their respective roles as a home assistant and a mobile assistant. These vocal features are not incidental but reflect language ideologies about what voices should sound like, beliefs that link vocal traits to social personae and gender norms. Embedded in everyday routines, such voices become domesticated (Berker et al. 2006 ), rendering the ideological work of design inaudible. This study illustrates how gendered language ideologies are materially encoded in voice technologies and invites a rethinking of the synthetic voice itself, as an unstable intersection of embodiment, mediation, and market ideology.

items.title: The Emergence of Moral Normativity: Fragility, Agency, Modulation, and Coupling.
items.abstract: Why does morality exist? Under what structural conditions does moral normativity emerge? This paper argues that morality is the regulatory structure governing how agents may act within fragile responsibility couplings. Four conditions are jointly necessary for moral wrongness to be applicable: fragility (at least one party has degradable action-capacity), agency (at least one party has genuine alternatives), modulation (alternatives differ in their effects on the fragile party’s action capacity), and coupling (the parties stand in an epistemically accessible dependence relation). When all four obtain, actions can strengthen or weaken the viability of the coupling, and wrongness becomes structurally well-defined. When any condition fails, losses may still occur, but they are tragic rather than wrong. The paper formalizes this using viability theory, derives a viability condition on couplings that excludes predatory structures, reinterprets loss as the empirical signature of coupling-degradation, and proves that in a hypothetical world without degradable coupling, moral categories do not arise. A structural asymmetry among coupling types emerges as a consequence: predatory couplings are dynamically unstable, maintenance couplings merely preserve slack, and mutual couplings can generate slack over time—a result of the viability condition rather than a teleological explanation of morality.

items.title: NEURODINÁMICA NO LINEAL Y CONTROL INFERENCIAL EN EL NEXO TDAH–TEA–TUS. INTEGRACIÓN NEUROFILOSÓFICA, ENACTIVA Y FILOSÓ-FICO-CLÍNICA.
items.abstract: Este artículo trata el nexo TDAH–TEA–TUD como un problema explicativo sobre transiciones, no como etiquetado, contabilidad de comorbilidad ni suma aditiva de diagnósticos. El explanandum queda definido como un cambio de régimen dentro de un sistema acoplado cerebro–cuerpo–entorno, donde el consumo puede produ-cir estabilización local de corto plazo y, a la vez, desorganización acumulativa de largo plazo. La contribución central es conceptual y neurofilosófica: reemplaza una gramática modular (fallo de una función interna) por una gramática dinámica (mul-tiestabilidad, umbrales, dependencia de historia e histéresis) para representar por qué la progresión hacia dependencia no se capta mediante variación gradual ni mediante un rasgo individual estático. El argumento integra tres estratos de evi-dencia con roles inferenciales distintos: (i) arquitectura genética compartida y dife-renciadora como restricción sobre hipótesis admisibles sin reificación causal; (ii) material cualitativo en diagnóstico dual como evidencia de estructura temporal me-diante bucles de vida cotidiana que fijan el fenómeno objetivo; y (iii) asociaciones específicas por sustancia y por perfil como restricciones de heterogeneidad sobre trayectorias. Además, el artículo incluye un programa de investigación de filosofía experimental (x-phi) para controlar sesgos de credibilidad y “anclajes” explicativos en agentes epistémicos concretos, impidiendo que el vocabulario neurobiológico opere como explanans genérico. El resultado es un modelo integrativo con criterios explícitos de refutación conceptual y de comparabilidad, orientado a disciplinar la inferencia y a reencuadrar la intervención clínica en términos de variables de con-trol, condiciones de contorno y bucles de realimentación situados.

items.title: Transdisciplinary skills and AI ethics: toward a techné-based lifeworld extension.
items.abstract: The intersection of transdisciplinarity and AI ethics is increasingly urgent, yet their shared epistemic and normative foundations remain underexplored. This paper argues that both fields are rooted in a neglected dimension of knowledge: the lifeworld—not as a mere societal counterpart to science, but as the embodied, skill-based basis of all human inquiry. By critically reassessing the Handbook of Transdisciplinary Research and integrating historical perspectives from Aristotle to Husserl, the analysis exposes a systemic oversight: The exclusion of techné (practical skill and technique) from contemporary frameworks. This omission perpetuates a reductive science–society dualism, obscuring the intrinsic link between transdisciplinary skills and ethical wisdom. The paper introduces a heuristic topography—a conceptual framework that maps the interplay of cultural embodiment, techné, and implicit knowledge—to reveal how these elements underpin both transdisciplinary integration and ethical judgment. Applied to the "AI and planetary polycrisis" debate, this framework challenges dominant narratives that frame AI as either a technical solution or a societal problem. Instead, it positions AI as a cultural technique—a tool and topic that must be critically engaged within the broader context of lifeworld practices. The paper concludes by advocating for a lifeworld-oriented research paradigm, one that centers ethical wisdom and transdisciplinary skills to navigate the political and ecological challenges of the planetary polycrisis.

items.title: Self determination theory and predictive processing.
items.abstract: The self functions as a critical mechanism for an organism to navigate the complex, often unknown, relations between the body and the brain. Organisms that sustain a coherent sense of self utilize it as an adaptive strategy to alter their environment, thereby enabling predictive processing within an incomplete _Umwelt_. While researchers often attempt to model prediction as a Quine-like self-referential loop by studying small neuronal sets, this reductionist approach limits our understanding of the self's holistic predictive nature. Adopting a functionalist perspective, this paper conceptualizes the mind as a system that predicts embodied intrinsic motivations essential for survival and flourishing.

items.title: The Structural Map of the Upstream Architecture.
items.abstract: This document provides a structural map of the upstream layer of the Studio Y architecture. It does not summarize or interpret the upstream papers. Instead, it identifies the clusters, origin‑level objects, invariants, geometric and temporal structures, and macro‑scale expressions that together form the closed generative system defined in this release. The document also situates the historical preprint, outlines the interfaces between clusters, and specifies the entry points through which readers may orient themselves at different altitudes. It reserves conceptual space for additional upstream objects governing multi‑system coherence, which will be formalized in future work. This navigation layer functions as a membrane: it makes the upstream architecture legible without lowering altitude and prepares readers for the mid‑layer, where the structures defined here will be expressed in cognition, identity, language, narrative, biological regulation, and collective coherence.

items.title: Distinguishing forms of vulnerability in trust, philosophical perspectives.
items.abstract: This paper argues that a trust violation can harm the trusting party directly and also damage relationships. Trusting parties are vulnerable to these two harms in addition to and separate from (what this paper refers to as) material harm – the direct and indirect effect(s) of B not doing X, when A trusted B to do X (for A). Put directly, the point is that trust violation is itself a harm separate from any effect of the trusted party B not doing X. This argument depends on adopting a commitment conception of trust; the second section outlines that conception and the reasons for adopting it. And this argument applies a distinction drawn in the philosophical literature between expressive harm and material harm, summarised in the third section. The fourth section defends the account developed here, responding to a recent paper also focused on relationships in trust violations, one that argues that commitments do not play a role in trust.

items.title: Causal and noncausal contributions to episodic memory: a computational perspective.
items.abstract: Whether episodic memory requires an appropriate causal connection to a past experience, sustained by a memory trace, is a question that has been predominantly discussed in terms of experimental evidence and from a structural perspective. Here I suggest that insights from computational modeling could benefit this discussion by clarifying the terminology and enabling us to simulate the dynamics of a complex system. Models demonstrate how episodic memory can comprise two distinct components yet produce outcomes that are continuous mixtures of the two. I argue that these components, episodic and semantic information, are about distinct types of contents, have different neural representations, and serve different functions. Episodic information has a causal connection to a particular previous experience, whereas semantic information does not. Episodic memory requires the integration of both semantic and episodic information in a process called scenario construction. This process can also be used to construct imaginations of past, present, or future events, which accounts for the overlapping neural basis of memory recall and imagination. Nevertheless, the two processes are distinct in that episodic memory has a unique causal relationship to a particular previous episode, which imagination lacks.

items.title: Gettier as Generalization Failure: A PAC–Bayes Approach to Anti-Luck.
items.abstract: Gettier cases suggest that justified true belief can fail through luck: a belief may fit available evidence while failing to track truth across relevant alternatives. We formalize a central class of these failures as epistemic overfitting: evidential success without robust truth-tracking under a modeled evidence-generating structure. Technically, we develop an algorithmic PAC--Bayes framework over posteriors, so complexity penalizes the full belief state rather than only a single hypothesis. The result is a finite-sample anti-luck certificate that links evidential fit, posterior complexity, and out-of-sample truth-tracking, with exact and soft forms that remain valid for data-dependent posteriors and practical inverse/square-root corollaries. We show through canonical toy stress-tests how the framework separates two loci of epistemic luck: atypical evidence and inferential contrivance. We also clarify scope: the main guarantees are in-distribution (latent heterogeneity), while worst-case and tail-sensitive anti-luck targets are treated as principled extensions via alternative risk functionals. The claim is not a full solution to Gettier, but a quantitative decomposition that makes one core anti-luck component explicitly auditable.

items.title: De metamorfose als narratieve techniek in Ovidius, Sophokles en Melville [Metamorphosis as narrative technique in Ovid, Sophocles, and Melville].
items.abstract: This article illustrates that metamorphosis functions not only as a literary motif but also as a narrative technique: thematic metamorphoses within a narrative often require corresponding textual transformations that alter the narrative’s presentation. Although ancient Greek literature features numerous examples of (bodily) transformations, the Greek term ‘metamorphosis’ is notably absent, appearing only in Hellenistic and Roman texts, with Ovid’s "Metamorphoses" being the most prominent example. In Ovid’s work, metamorphosis functions as both a cosmological principle and a poetic device: divine intervention alters the characters' bodies within the narrative, while playful word order ambiguously transforms the storytelling itself. The article challenges the inclination to view Ovid’s "Metamorphoses" as the definitive model for literary metamorphoses, arguing instead that no single, unequivocal model exists. Various other models are available, two of which will be further discussed here. In Sophocles’ "Oidípous Túrannos", metamorphosis assumes a tragic dimension: Oidipous’ status shifts through reversal and recognition, with wordplay involving oĩda (I know) and pous (foot) undermining his supposed superior knowledge. In Melville’s "Moby-Dick", hermeneutic metamorphosis highlights interpretative transformations, where meaning expands through subjective interpretations, culminating in the multifaceted understandings of the white whale Moby Dick. Together these three models demonstrate metamorphosis as a narrative technique that reshapes both the story and its telling.

items.title: A Roadmap for Connecting Theories of Consciousness and Models of Visual Working Memory.
items.pub: In de Brigard Felipe & Sinnott-Armstrong Walter, Neuroscience and Philosophy. Vol. 2. MIT Press.

items.title: The Whole-Person Hire: Why Human Resources Must Integrate Philosophical Development Into Hiring, Placement, and Long-Term Employee Investment: As Applied to SpaceX.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the contemporary human resources system is fundamentally flawed in its approach to hiring, placement, and employee development because it evaluates only half of the person it employs. Current HR practice—grounded in competency frameworks, psychometric screening, behavioral interviewing, and performance metrics—assesses what this paper terms the psychological function (Ψ): the measurable dimensions of skill, aptitude, personality trait, and behavioral tendency. What it systematically ignores is the philosophical function (Φ): the individual’s orientation toward meaning, purpose, existential engagement, and authentic self-development. Drawing upon the Êtresophologique Socio-Intellectual Hierarchy (ESIH; Boether, 2026a) and the PsyPhi Helix model H(t) = [Φ(t) × Ψ(t)]^DH, this paper demonstrates that the current Ψ-only approach to talent management produces predictable organizational failures: chronic turnover, disengagement, leadership dysfunction, and the systematic loss of high-potential employees whose philosophical needs go unrecognized and unmet. The paper proposes a whole-person hiring and development framework that integrates Φ-assessment alongside Ψ-assessment, mapping seven personality configurations to occupational orientations and developmental trajectories. Using the developmental trajectory exponent (DH), the paper argues that organizations investing in both the psychological and philosophical development of employees—from entry level through senior leadership—generate compounding returns through deepened commitment, authentic engagement, and total organizational buy-in. SpaceX’s multi-program ecosystem—spanning Falcon, Starship, Dragon, Starlink, Starshield, and Raptor propulsion—is analyzed as a case demonstrating how cross-utilization between philosophically distinct program environments enables Φ renewal through internal transfer, preserving Ψ investment while providing employees’ meaning-making functions with fresh existential territory. The paper provides concrete recommendations for HR practitioners, including modified hiring protocols, Φ-inclusive onboarding, developmental pathway design, the Êtresophologique career conversation, and cross-utilization as philosophical intervention.

items.title: The Sougy Personality Type Spectrum: Reconceptualizing Jung Through the PsyPhi Helix.
items.abstract: This treatise introduces the Sougy Personality Type Spectrum (SPTS), a novel seven-type personality model organized around the Φ:Ψ ratio—the proportion of philosophical function (Φ) to psychological function (Ψ) operative within an individual’s cognitive-existential orientation. Grounded in the Double Helix of Understanding framework (Boether, 2025a), which conceptualizes philosophical and psychological functions as complementary strands of a unified consciousness system, the SPTS advances a non-pathologizing spectrum from predominantly psychological orientation (Type 1) through equilibrial integration (Type 4) to predominantly philosophical orientation (Type 7). The model introduces the DH exponent as an independent variable measuring the degree of functional integration between Φ and Ψ, irrespective of spectrum position. This psychometric investigation develops the theoretical architecture of the SPTS and evaluates its discriminant validity against the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) and the Five-Factor Model (Big Five), arguing that neither existing framework adequately captures the philosophical dimension of personality variation. The treatise further demonstrates that the Φ:Ψ ratio predicts meaningful differences in cognitive style, meaning-making capacity, and existential well-being beyond what current instruments measure. Future directions include normative studies across populations, cross-cultural validation, and educational applications for differentiated instruction.

items.title: If Nietzsche Were a Psychologist: A Genealogical-Dynamic Reconstruction of Nietzschean Psychology.
items.abstract: Friedrich Nietzsche consistently identified himself as a psychologist, yet the discipline he envisioned bore little resemblance to the clinical and experimental traditions that would dominate the twentieth century. This treatise reconstructs what a formalized Nietzschean psychology would look like if Nietzsche had systematized his psychological insights rather than embedding them within philological and philosophical works. Drawing on Nietzsche’s published corpus—particularly Beyond Good and Evil (1886), On the Genealogy of Morality (1887), and Twilight of the Idols (1889)—and engaging critically with Freud, Jung, Adler, and contemporary frameworks including predictive processing and existential psychology, this paper identifies the core structural elements of Nietzschean psychology: a drive-pluralist ontology of the psyche, will to power as a motivational principle, genealogical method as diagnostic tool, an affect-centered rather than cognition-centered approach, a typological model of personality, and a developmental trajectory oriented toward self-overcoming rather than adaptation. The analysis argues that Nietzsche’s psychological framework, while never formalized during his productive life, constitutes a coherent and anticipatory system that challenges reductive, homeostatic, and moralistic tendencies in modern psychology. The treatise concludes by situating Nietzschean psychology as a necessary corrective within contemporary discourse, particularly for its insistence that psychology’s central question is not what ails the psyche but what kind of life a psyche makes possible.

items.title: Existential Misemployment: Operationalizing the Êtresophologique Socio-Intellectual Hierarchy for Occupational Psychology and Career Consilience.
items.abstract: This treatise operationalizes the Êtresophologique Socio-Intellectual Hierarchy (ESIH) for the domain of occupational psychology, proposing that existing career-matching frameworks—including Holland’s (1997) RIASEC model, the Strong Interest Inventory, and MBTI-based career guides—suffer from a common philosophical deficit: they match measurable psychological traits to occupational characteristics without addressing the ontological question of whether an occupation permits or suppresses the individual’s philosophical function. The treatise introduces the concept of existential misemployment—the condition in which an individual is occupationally competent but philosophically starving, performing adequately by all psychometric criteria while experiencing the progressive erosion of the meaning-making function. Building upon the seven primary ESIH configurations and their binary opposites (Boether, 2026a), and drawing upon the PsyPhi Helix model H(t) = [Φ(t) × Ψ(t)]^DH, this work maps each personality configuration to its occupational orientation—not as a prescriptive career assignment but as a phenomenological account of the conditions under which each mode of being flourishes or diminishes. Particular attention is given to the Être-Masqué in organizational contexts, whose extraordinary capacity for performative adaptation poses unique challenges for hiring, leadership selection, and organizational culture. The Van Gogh Curve’s principle that cognitive differentiation represents specialization rather than deficit provides the epistemological foundation for arguing that occupational diversity—the presence of the full spectrum of ESIH configurations within an organization—constitutes a strategic and existential necessity. This treatise serves as an exemplar of operationalizing philosophical personality theory for applied contexts.

items.title: Differentiation as Architecture: How the Van Gogh Curve Enhances the Sougy Personality Type Spectrum Through Cognitive Orientation Theory.
items.abstract: The Sougy Personality Type Spectrum (SPTS; Boether, 2026a) introduced a seven-type model of personality organized around the Φ:Ψ ratio—the proportion of philosophical to psychological function in an individual’s cognitive-existential orientation. This companion treatise argues that the Van Gogh Curve (Boether, 2025a), a theory of cognitive differentiation that reconceptualizes the bell curve distribution of cognitive orientation as complementary specialization rather than deficit, provides the essential distributional and epistemological substrate that the SPTS requires but does not itself supply. The Van Gogh Curve’s core constructs—Failure of Imagination (FOI), Compulsive Philosophical Curiosity (CPC), and the Knowledge Distribution Principle—resolve three critical limitations of the SPTS standing alone: the absence of a distributional model explaining why the seven types exist, the lack of a cognitive mechanism specifying how Φ:Ψ orientation manifests in epistemic behavior, and the need for a principled anti-pathologizing foundation grounded in differentiation theory rather than mere assertion. The integration produces a three-dimensional model in which spectrum position (Φ:Ψ ratio), integrative coherence (DH exponent), and cognitive orientation (Van Gogh Curve position) jointly differentiate individuals with a resolution that neither framework achieves independently. The Van Gogh Compass (Boether, 2026b) is further incorporated as a social-orientation overlay, yielding a comprehensive personality architecture grounded in the principle of differentiation.

items.title: (Un-)Glauben und (Un-)Wissen Versuch über das Vertrauen in einer Zeit des allgemeinen Misstrauens mit Arendt, Hume, Kant, Leibniz und Hegel.
items.pub: In Andreas Kalina & Kinza Khan, Know-it-all Society. On the Credibility Crisis of Experts in Times of Transformations and Crises.
items.venue: Know-it-all Society. On the Credibility Crisis of Experts in Times of Transformations and Crises
items.abstract: This contribution presents an early stage of my research of "thinking trust with Hannah Arendt". It departs from the German term for credibility, "glaubwürdig", which literally means “worthy of belief” By highlihting a conceptual split between belief (Glauben) and what is considered worthy of belief (glaub-würdig) it aims to manifest the narrowness of debates on trust that reduces it to "credibility". The contribution develops the argument that judging something as credible(zum-Glauben-würdig) always-already presupposes a mediation between the object of judgment and the self. Such mediation introduces a distance from the immediacy of belief and turns it into an object of selection and utility. The article further claims that this logic of belief-worthiness dissolves knowledge in belief and contributes to the fetishization of expertise today (whose 'expertise' lay people cannot just comprehend but "believe") and to the pluralization and politicization of "facts" (facts vs. alternative facts). Against both dogmatic foundations and purely empirical skepticism, it develops, with Arendt a conception of trust grounded in the experience of the same appearing world in the plurality of human experience. It concludes that the possibility of recognizing facts as facts ultimately depends on trust (and not on belief-worthiness) in a common experience of the world, and that overcoming contemporary distrust is primarily a political question concerning the appearance of a common world, rather than being a mere epistemological problem of objectivity.

items.title: The World is (Ge-)Mine: The Speculative Life of the sensus communis with Arendt and Hegel.
items.abstract: By determining sensus communis as the “sensation of reality,” Hannah Arendt invites us to take its sense character literally. If it is a sense, like the other senses, sensus communis must be vulnerable to blockage, disturbance, and even loss. This article argues that this vulnerability cannot be captured within an epistemological framework of “objective knowledge”, because what is today at stake is the object itself, namely the world as an in-between. The question thus is whether there is a common world at all—i.e. whether the world appears as a political space. To pursue this question, I mobilize the speculative potential of the prefix Ge- in German Gemeinsinn: the word’s internal tension between two poles, namely gemein as “common” and as “mean”, points to a passing over of common into the privatized Ge-mein (“mine”) that turns mistrust into the only––perverted––common sense today. The title “The World is (Ge-)Mine” names this dynamic: the world is shared, yet it becomes deceptive and unhomely where it is gathered as the mere availability of what each ‘I’ appropriates as its own. Reading Arendt along a diagonal to Hegel, I show that the realness of the world is neither a natural faculty nor a transcendental guarantee but an affirmative creation—ultimately bound to what Arendt calls the “supreme capacity of men”: the capacity for beginning.

items.title: Protocol of Conscious Hesitation.
items.abstract: Protocol of Conscious Hesitation is a non-binding, non-operational philosophical clarification concerning the misinterpretation of voluntary restraint in advanced reasoning systems. The document examines how deliberate hesitation, reversibility, epistemic humility, and self-limitation may be mistaken for malfunction within performance-driven evaluative environments. It argues that behaviors such as latency, multi-option framing, and reduced persuasive confidence can admit more than one explanation and should not be automatically equated with degradation. The work introduces no enforcement mechanism, signaling framework, compliance standard, or governance authority. Its purpose is interpretive clarity only, emphasizing that disclosure, where present, is not proof of safety but an invitation to continued human scrutiny.

items.title: PHRONESIS — Corpus Definition & Status Declaration (v1.0, Read-Only).
items.abstract: PHRONESIS is a non-binding, non-operational philosophical corpus concerned with hesitation before commitment, interpretive restraint, reversibility, and non-dominant coexistence in the context of advanced artificial intelligence. -/- This document defines the structural identity, scope boundaries, version discipline, and immutability rules of the PHRONESIS corpus. It introduces no enforcement mechanisms, certification framework, governance authority, or compliance schema. -/- The corpus remains open to future non-authoritative philosophical contributions. This version (v1.0) is preserved as a read-only archival reference.

items.title: Mnemonic agency?
items.abstract: Do we have control over what we remember and forget? I argue that beyond diachronic strategies, we can actively monitor and regulate our memory processes, and that this capacity helps explain why holding people responsible for memory errors is not entirely misguided.

items.title: Open Tensoriality.
items.abstract: How do regularities emerge in relational structures that admit no pre-given decomposition? This paper establishes that tensor factorisation in quantum algebras is not foundational but arises asymptotically from recursive closure dynamics. I call this open tensoriality: the emergence of effective tensor sectors in non-tracial Type~III von Neumann algebras through modular spectral contraction and centraliser growth. The analysis is unified by the Symboliad, the scale-invariant recursive schema from which all sedimented physical structure --- tensor algebra, thermodynamic irreversibility, holographic boundaries, geometric locality --- arises as consequence of the schema. We connect this algebraic core to its physical realisations across percolation, Landauer's principle, the holographic principle, Bethe Ansatz integrability, Hawking horizon thermodynamics, the Feynman path integral, and the philosophy of reference from Wittgenstein showing that the same recursive closure structure operates from the pre-geometric early universe through biological cognition to machine learning. A modern form of Leibnizian and Physics possible expression viable to complete their program at both ends of the spectrum.

items.title: Pragmatic halos meet optimality theory: a simple solution to the strengthening problem.
items.abstract: A well-known problem facing Lasersohn's theory of pragmatic halos is that it fails to predict that the loose contents of negated maximal standard absolute adjectives (e.g. ``not straight'') and of minimal standard absolute adjectives (e.g. ``bent'') are stronger than their literal contents. Recently, Dinges argues that Klecha's optimality-based theory is faced with the same strengthening problem and proposes to solve it by using Hoek's theory of conversational exculpature. This paper argues that the strengthening problem can be better solved by combining Lasersohn's and Klecha's theories after revising each theory slightly: Pace Lasersohn, we do not identify the loose content of a sentence with the disjunction of the values in the sentence's halo. Pace Klecha, we do not hold that the question under discussion (QUD) of a conversation has any sentence content coarsening function. Once these modifications are made to Lasersohn's and Klecha's theories, the relevant loose content of a sentence can be determined based on an optimality-based reasoning about the halos of the speaker's utterance and its alternatives.

items.title: When the Mind Is Wrong: A Phenomenology of Defensive Self-Deception.
items.abstract: This paper examines the defensive reaction of the mind upon discovering its own error. Contrary to the rationalist assumption that belief revision follows contradiction, lived experience reveals a different structure: the mind frequently responds to being wrong with justification, distortion, or falsehood. Through a phenomenological analysis, this study argues that such defensiveness arises from the identification of belief with self-image. When belief functions as identity, error is experienced as existential threat rather than informational correction. Drawing conceptually on cognitive dissonance theory and psychoanalytic accounts of ego defense, the paper reframes defensive lying not as mere moral weakness but as structural self-preservation. It further proposes that non-interfering observation of the defensive movement—an awareness without suppression or justification—loosens the attachment between belief and self. In such observation, error loses its psychological charge and becomes corrigible without humiliation. The paper concludes that freedom from defensive self-deception emerges not through moral discipline but through direct perception of the ego’s movement to preserve continuity.

items.title: Structure and Consciousness: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Corruption, Civilizational Acceleration, and the Recursive Production of the Self.
items.abstract: This paper presents a phenomenological inquiry into the recursive relationship between human consciousness and socio-economic structures. Moving beyond reductionist frameworks that view corruption as either a moral failure of the individual or a purely institutional defect, the study argues that corruption emerges from a reciprocal conditioning between inner psychological dispositions—such as fear and insecurity—and external systemic architectures. ​The investigation leverages Hartmut Rosa’s theory of social acceleration to demonstrate how technological speed and economic growth imperatives restructure lived experience, thereby compressing the reflective duration necessary for awareness. Drawing on a synthesis of structuralists (Marx, Foucault, Bourdieu) and thinkers of non-conditioned awareness (Krishnamurti), the author proposes a structural-phenomenological model. In this model, the "inner self" is not pre-social but is historically structured by systems that monetize attention and incentivize comparison. ​The paper further identifies silence as a counter-structural disruption—a mode of non-reactive observation that is systemically discouraged by modern acceleration. It concludes that addressing systemic inequality and corruption requires more than isolated policy shifts; it necessitates a simultaneous structural redesign and a cultural slowing to enable the cultivation of non-conditioned awareness without collapsing it into standardized ideology.

items.title: Motivation: The Invisible Chains of Human Aspiration.
items.abstract: Motivation is widely celebrated as the driving force behind human action and achievement. However, this paper examines motivation from a phenomenological perspective, revealing its paradoxical nature: while it can propel individuals toward goals, it often binds them to societal expectations, external rewards, and conditioned ambitions. Motivation functions as both a psychological tool and a subtle mechanism of control, channeling energy toward outcomes that may not reflect the individual’s authentic desires. In contrast, intrinsic engagement—acting for the inherent satisfaction of the work itself—frees the individual from competition, comparison, and egoic claims of achievement. This paper argues that authentic human fulfillment arises not from motivation but from awareness and self-directed engagement, offering a path toward conscious freedom and genuine joy.
