By prioritizing attention capture, algorithmic personalization, and digital validation, these platforms gradually replace reflection with reaction and authenticity with performance. The result is not an overt suppression of freedom, but a silent conditioning of consciousness in which individuals unknowingly outsource their thinking and self-concept to digital systems. The article contends that the central issue is not the existence of social media itself, but its unconscious use, and calls for greater psychological awareness and critical digital literacy to preserve individuality in an age of invisible influence.

items.title: Who owns meaning in an age of AI? Beyond transparent systems to shared cosmologies.
items.abstract: AI governance in healthcare increasingly foregrounds transparency, auditability, and traceability. Yet what these frameworks often secure is a surface-level domain of factual correctness and accountable documentation—what this paper terms the semantic meaning layer (SML). In clinical practice, however, trust and ethical acceptability are also anchored in deeper, slower-moving structures: cultural cosmologies, value commitments, embodied practices, and lived experience—what this paper terms the cosmological meaning layer (CML). A key risk in contemporary deployment is, therefore, not only “factual hallucination” but “meaning hallucination”: outputs that are technically coherent yet ethically hollow, socially misaligned, or experientially discordant. The paper proposes the SML–CML framework as a co-constituted stratification: analytically distinguishable but not ontologically separable. Drawing on abductive clinical reasoning—especially traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) pattern differentiation—we show how diagnosis is often an act of meaning-construction shaped by embodied perception (touch, trained attention) and shared worldviews, not merely an inferential mapping from data to labels. We then clarify “whose trust” transparency regimes often secure, distinguishing relational trust (patient–clinician) from institutional legitimacy (audit, regulation, medico-legal protection). Finally, we show how global coding infrastructures (e.g., ICD-11) and AI evaluation practices can strengthen comparability while structurally excluding local cosmologies and embodied meaning. We argue that preventing AI-induced hollowing of meaning requires governance that explicitly addresses worldview pluralism and supports “shared abduction”: collaborative, value-explicit inquiry in which humans and institutions negotiate not only correctness but also the cosmologies that make care meaningful.

items.title: Meditazioni kaneane. Il teatro di Sarah Kane: la malattia nell'essere e la psicopatologia fenomenologica.
items.abstract: In this paper, I offer a phenomenological meditation on Sarah Kane’s theatre, exploring mental illness as illness of existential being. To do so, I bring into dialogue personal lived experience and phenomenological psychopathology, depicting a particular form of literarian articulation of experiences that I define 'theatre of Erlebnisse'. The aim is not to construct a systematic philosophical interpretation of Kane’s work as though it were a theoretical edifice, but rather to navigate its tensions through phenomenological tools that seek to contemplate the complexity of its interwoven dimensions of psychopathology, literature, and aesthetic outrage.

items.title: Back‑End Law Revisited: From a Four‑Stage Collapse Model to a Two‑Force Equation of Identity Transformation.
items.abstract: The Back End Law was originally formulated as a four stage model of identity transformation, describing Collapse, Threshold, Irreversibility, and Reorganization as sequential phases triggered by extreme psychological pressure. This earlier formulation successfully captured the phenomenology of transformation across historical, spiritual, and creative domains. However, it did not fully explain why individuals exposed to similar collapse pressures diverge so dramatically in their outcomes, nor why low PHI individuals sometimes achieve improbable recoveries. This paper introduces a revised formulation, the Final Equation, which reframes the Back End Law as a two force interaction between the Pressure of Collapse and Structural Integrity (PHI), with External Scaffolding functioning as a stabilizing modifier. While the original four stage model remains descriptively valuable, the Final Equation provides a more parsimonious, predictive, and falsifiable account of transformation outcomes. The equation demonstrates that collapse outcomes are determined by the ratio of effective structural integrity to collapse pressure, thereby explaining stable reorganizations, failed reorganizations, and Black Swan recoveries within a single structural framework. The model is illustrated through three applied cases: Nelson Mandela (stable reorganization), Friedrich Nietzsche (failed reorganization), and John Nash (Black Swan recovery). The Final Equation thus unifies the descriptive richness of the original model with the explanatory precision of a physics like structural law. In fact, for centuries, the study of profound human transformation—from spiritual awakening to psychological breakdown—has lacked a unified, predictive model. Experiences of genius, sainthood, and madness have been treated as separate, often inexplicable phenomena. This paper introduces a new, falsifiable paradigm: The Final Equation of the Back-End Law. We propose that the outcome of any major life crisis or breakthrough is not random, but is a predictable result determined by the ratio between the Pressure of Collapse (P_collapse) and the system's Effective Integrity (Φ_eff). Effective Integrity is defined as the sum of an individual's baseline internal coherence (Structural Integrity, Φ_structure) and the coherence provided by their environment (External Scaffolding, S_external). By analyzing case studies of a Stable Reboot (Nelson Mandela), a Failed Reboot (Friedrich Nietzsche), and a Black Swan …

items.title: Freedom of Thought as Economic Infrastructure: Why High-Tech Capital Requires a Complex Subject.
items.abstract: This article offers an ontodynamic interpretation of contemporary technological capitalism within the framework of metamonism. It is argued that the expansion of capital into high-technology domains is structurally impossible without the formation of a cognitively complex subject capable of abstraction, tolerance of uncertainty, and autonomous differentiation. Freedom of thought is examined not as a humanistic value, but as a functional economic infrastructure enabling continuous production of variability (Diff). Subsequently, this same freedom is deconstructed as a form of high-frequency Lógos capture: capital does not liberate difference but accelerates its alienation and commodification. Authoritarianism and liberal capitalism are analyzed as distinct frequency regimes of Lógos — low-frequency and high-frequency — both colonial with respect to Mónos. In the concluding section, an ontodynamic tactic for the node is proposed: not the search for an alternative system, but local non-recognizability as the limit of profiling. Mónos is conceived not as a territory or state, but as a temporary failure of recognition — an event that escapes circulation.

items.title: Epochē as Asymptotic Approximation to the Forbidden Attractor: An Ontodynamic Interpretation in Metamonism.
items.abstract: In the phenomenological tradition, epochē is conceived as an act of liberation of consciousness from naturalistic presuppositions, opening access to the “pure givenness” of the phenomenon. This article proposes an ontodynamic reinterpretation of this practice within the framework of metamonism — a proto-ontology grounded in the prohibition of absolute self-identity and the necessity of continuous differentiation. Epochē here appears not as the disclosure of the ground of being, but as an asymptotic approximation of the cognitive node to the forbidden attractor Fix — a structural singularity of the process, ontologically equivalent to Nothing. The analysis demonstrates that epochē functions as a local minimization of differentiation (Diff), redistributing the process into pre-symbolic registers, and serves as a phase of retuning within the general flow of Λffffffff, rather than its telos. Thus, metamonism removes the metaphysical claim of epochē, returning it to the productive dynamics of differences.

items.title: Beyond Chance and Necessity: Replicative Variability and the Constraint Guided Dynamics of Evolution.
items.abstract: Abstract This paper develops a non teleological metaphysics of biological evolution by reframing replication as intrinsic generative variability and evolutionary outcomes as constraint generated local optima. The traditional vocabulary of “mutation,” “error,” and “fidelity” imports teleological assumptions that are incompatible with the empirical realities of replication, development, and morphological organisation. Drawing on molecular biology, developmental systems theory, and recent work on bioelectric patterning, we argue that variability is not accidental but constitutive: replication is a stochastic generative process whose variability is evolutionarily tuned, and development is the stabilisation of morphological attractors within a constraint defined landscape. This framework dissolves the classical dichotomy between chance and necessity by showing that variation is structured stochasticity and selection is the expression of constraint architecture. Integrating insights from Deacon’s constraint based causation, Noble’s systems biology, and Levin’s work on bioelectric control of form, we propose a unified metaphysics of life grounded in constraint bounded generativity and the impulse for persistence. If correct, this reframing has implications for every biological discipline, from genetics to ecology, and provides a coherent conceptual foundation for understanding the emergence, stability, and creativity of living systems.

items.title: Infinite Deferral, Personal Ground, and Love as Terminal Closure: A Grounding–Agency–Relational Fixed-Point Synthesis.
items.abstract: We synthesize a structural chain linking (i) the metaphysical impossibility of infinite causal/grounding deferral, (ii) a conditional consequence of libertarian personhood for the nature of the non-derivative ground, and (iii) a formally unique terminal relational closure among persons. First, we argue that an infinite regress of wholly derivative existents cannot instantiate concrete reality under a defended well-foundedness axiom for grounding over concreta, yielding the existence of a non-derivative ground. Second, conditional on libertarian agency, we prove a strengthened exhaustion-dilemma: a purely impersonal base yields only deterministic or stochastic outputs, and any alleged “strong emergence” of libertarian authorship either collapses into those outputs or requires a non-impersonal primitive. Third, we replace informal taxonomies of relational modes with an exhaustive conditional/unconditional partition of standing-conferral and prove that every conditional standing relation is ω-open under libertarian freedom, while non-relation and unilateral affirmation fail full-resolution. This yields unconditional mutual affirmation (“love”) as the unique non-coercive terminal closure configuration. We then separate fixed-point existence (Knaster–Tarski) from uniqueness (a structural ω-openness elimination theorem), and present a dynamical refinement: for finite populations, a defect potential decreases under a minimal, non-coercive update rule derived from the ω-openness constraint, yielding convergence to total affirmation. The result is offered as a conditional theorem-schema within contemporary grounding theory and agency metaphysics rather than as a freestanding proof of any particular theological doctrine.

items.title: Book Review: Theodore Gracyk's Making Meaning in Popular Song: Philosophical Essays. [REVIEW]
items.pub: Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism.
items.venue: Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism
items.abstract: Now is a great time to be working in philosophy of popular music. Work is currently being done on rap and hip-hop, pop, E.D.M., country, metal, and punk. Besides this, the problem-space of popular music in general is growing as well. Topics of interest across all of these genres include the nature of versioning, the metaphysics of musical groups, hooks, and groove, among others. If there is any one scholar within analytic philosophy who can take credit for this explosion of work, it is Theodore Gracyk. Gracyk’s pioneering Rhythm and Noise (1996) definitively carved the philosophy of popular music off from the philosophy of music and the rest is, in many ways, history. Now, almost twenty years later, he has followed that work up with Making Meaning in Popular Song (2023), a collection of nine updated but previously published essays from between 2007 and 2017. This new collection, spanning ten years of work, brings together a variety of different threads and places them all into a larger context alongside one another. The emerging picture shows us a more complete vision of Gracyk’s pragmatics-driven philosophy of popular music. It is worth pointing out that the book recently won the American Society for Aesthetics Outstanding Monograph Prize, a fitting recognition of Gracyk’s enormous contributions to the philosophy of popular music. In what follows, I will very briefly summarize these essays in order, after which I will discuss the merits of the book along with one particular critical concern.

items.title: Cosmic Ontoenergetics: A Process-Based Framework for Understanding Consciousness in Thermodynamically Open Systems.
items.abstract: This paper develops Cosmic Ontoenergetics—a metaphysical framework that reconceptualizes the relationship between energy, structural complexity, and consciousness in thermodynamically open systems. I propose that phenomenal consciousness is the intrinsic nature of highly integrated energetic-informational processes sustained by continuous cosmic energy input. The framework integrates two complementary theories: the Theory of Open Cosmic Energy Supply (TOCES), which establishes that Earth as a thermodynamically open system continuously receives and accumulates energy in structural forms; and the Theory of Cosmic Ontoenergetics (TCO), which provides a metaphysical account of how energy flow through dissipative structures gives rise to increasingly complex forms of organization, culminating in systems capable of phenomenal awareness. By positing consciousness as the intrinsic nature of highly organized energetic structures, this process-based monism dissolves certain conceptual barriers in the mind-body problem without relying on dualism or reductive physicalism. The approach remains consistent with contemporary science while avoiding the pitfalls of both eliminativism and mysterianism, and generates philosophically significant predictions about the necessary conditions for consciousness. The framework offers three core contributions: first, an energetic ontology that takes energy transformations as ontologically basic, replacing substance-based metaphysics; second, a bridge between philosophy of mind and philosophy of physics through the concept of dissipative structures in open systems; and third, a naturalistic account of directionality in evolution toward complexity and awareness that avoids vitalism while preserving teleonomic explanations.

items.title: Persistent Internal Standpoints in Artificial Systems: Part 8 - Standpoint Without Sensorimotor Embodiment.
items.abstract: Embodied and enactive approaches frequently maintain that genuine standpoint requires sensorimotor embodiment, that is, interaction with an environment through mechanisms of sensing and movement. Contemporary artificial systems, however, range from purely informational architectures to robotically embodied agents. This paper evaluates embodiment within the architectural framework developed in earlier work. It argues that sensorimotor embodiment, whether biological or robotic, is not a necessary condition for the existence of a persistent internal standpoint. The minimal structural conditions for standpoint – persistence, structured internal geometry, closed-loop modulation, and trajectory-dependence – are internal organizational features. Quantia, artificial desire, and deliberation likewise do not require embodiment as a prerequisite. Embodiment functions as an enrichment of internal geometry rather than as its generative source. The grounding objection is addressed through the quantia framework, which supports organization-relative normativity grounded in internal closure rather than environmental coupling.

items.title: Three Non-Religious Models of Evil: Telos, Law, and Genealogy.
items.abstract: This paper develops a non-theological framework for analyzing “evil” by separating three levels that are often conflated in ordinary moral discourse: explanation (mechanisms), norm (impermissibility), and responsibility (attribution of guilt). It proposes a minimal typology of evil as behavior—impulsive, instrumental, and coalitionary—arguing that many philosophical disputes talk past one another because they silently target different behavioral regimes. The paper then tests three classical non-religious grounds of normativity—telos (Aristotle), law (Kant), and genealogy (Nietzsche)—showing that each functions as a distinct optic with characteristic strengths and blind spots across the three behavioral types. A neuro-evolutionary perspective is introduced as a realism-enhancing layer at the level of explanation, without reducing moral prohibition to biology. To avoid the naturalistic fallacy, the paper articulates two explicit normative anchors compatible with equal moral status: (1) evil as the destruction of agency (systematic objectification of persons) and (2) evil as the destruction of the conditions of cooperation (erosion of trust, predictability, reciprocity, and fair risk distribution). The resulting operational scheme treats evil not as a metaphysical essence but as reproducible regimes that can be recognized, constrained, and reduced without converting society into a machine of total control.

items.title: Cognitive-System Phenomenology — A Critique of Husserl (part 28).
items.abstract: In the previous section, we introduced the concept of a cognitive-system community. Our primary interest lies in those cognitive-system communities that are related to language. As mentioned earlier, even a particular dialect can constitute a cognitive-system community. Thus, we can see that there are in fact many such communities associated with language. At the same time, with the development of technology, we are now able to translate more and more languages instantly, thereby enabling communication between people who use different languages. As a result, the number of people with whom we can directly communicate through language continues to grow. Consequently, cognitive-system communities associated with globally prevalent languages will also expand. In this section, we will discuss the differences and connections between language-based cognitive-system communities and Husserl’s lifeworld. We will also briefly touch upon the process of knowledge transmission within a cognitive-system community. Clearly, a more comprehensive study is required for the problem of the development of cognitive systems, and I intend to return to this topic for further research when time permits. We have also discussed three types of relationships among members of a cognitive-system community and introduced the concepts of binary isomorphism, ternary isomorphism, and quaternary isomorphism.

items.title: Beyond-Man and Relational Agency: A Reading of Zarathustra through Attachment Theory.
items.abstract: This paper presents a structural reading of Nietzsche’s Thus Spoke Zarathustra as a theory of the self, contrasting it with John Bowlby’s attachment theory. It argues that Zarathustra embodies an agency derived from insecure-avoidant relational structures, characterized by unmodulated resolution, unilateral assertion, and isolation. While aesthetically compelling, this model appears structurally unsustainable when considered as a general guide to human development. By highlighting the absence of secure relational grounding and affective co-regulation, the analysis clarifies structural limitations in Nietzsche’s conception of self and suggests a possible integration of relationally moderated agency with the pursuit of self-overcoming. This reading is structural and interpretive; it does not intend to offer a historical or biographical psychological diagnosis of Nietzsche or his characters. -/- .

items.title: Why “Proving Consciousness” Isn’t the Right Question: A Resolution Theory View of the Hard Problem.
items.abstract: The Hard Problem asks why any physical or computational process should be accompanied by subjective experience. Resolution Theory (RT) does not claim to solve that metaphysical question. Instead it argues that “proving consciousness” is often the wrong governance target: third-person explanation and first-person standpoint answer different kinds of questions, and the absence of metaphysical certainty cannot be allowed to function as a policy veto. RT replaces the demand to derive qualia with an architectural criterion for when consciousness and agency become morally risky to ignore: a continuing subject that resolves uncertainty into commitment (authorship) under unavoidable exposure across time. Exposure is not “karma”; it is contact with reality—resolutions export effects into the shared world that can expand or contract option-space, for self and others. The paper distinguishes functional valence (control-relevant cost/benefit registration) from felt valence (phenomenal character), treating the gap as potentially deep while non-load-bearing for responsibility and safety design. It introduces a conservation principle: rollback cannot erase reality’s effects, only displace their ownership upstream—making authorship laundering by reset ethically charged in any human-impacting domain.

items.title: The Persistence Operator: Geometric Invariants in the Transmission of Meaning.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Persistence Operator, the mathematical object that explains how meaning survives discontinuity. Whereas the Meaning‑Formation Dynamical System (Object 1) governs the formation of coherence, the Persistence Operator formalizes the geometric invariants that allow meaning to re‑manifest across changing carriers, contexts, and time. The operator is defined by three components — the Gate, the Sentinel, and the Longitudinal Snap — which together determine when a structure can be recognized and conserved across rupture. Persistence is a thresholded, carrier‑independent process: meaning reappears when the receiving system meets the structural conditions for recognition, and dissipates when those conditions fail. This paper establishes the operator’s axioms, threshold mechanics, and interfaces with formation and transformation within the broader foundational architecture.

items.title: The Metabolic Manifold: The Isomorphism Operator and the Transformation of Tension.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Metabolic Manifold, the mathematical object that explains how systems transform raw tension into stable coherence. Whereas the Meaning‑Formation Dynamical System (Object 1) governs formation and the Persistence Operator (Object 2) governs survival across carriers, the Metabolic Manifold formalizes the process layer that enables both. It defines three components — the Isomorphism Operator, the Metabolic Engine, and the Greenhouse — which together determine how tension is buffered, aligned, and converted into stable invariants. The Metabolic Manifold explains how Ache becomes structure, how identity remains continuous across internal change, and how coherence becomes metabolically sustainable across time and contexts.

items.title: The Foundational Architecture of Meaning‑Formation.
items.abstract: This document presents the foundational architecture of meaning‑formation: a triad of mathematical objects that formalize the formation, survival, and transformation of meaning across systems, carriers, and time. Together, these objects constitute the first unified physics of meaning — a structural, metabolic, and geometric account of how coherence emerges, persists, and evolves.

items.title: ONTOLOGICAL DENSITY THEORY.
items.abstract: Ontological Density Theory: Emergent Realism and the Stratification of Social Reality -/- This paper introduces Ontological Density Theory, a framework for understanding how socially constructed entities achieve real ontological status and varying degrees of causal efficacy. Drawing on the social construction theory of Berger and Luckmann, Durkheim's analysis of ritual and social facts, Latour's actor-network theory, and phenomenological traditions, the theory makes a distinctive ontological claim: high-density social entities are not merely epistemological constructs but emergent relational structures with genuine causal powers. Ontological density is defined as the degree to which a given entity or relational system organizes and dominates the field of experience and action through the coordinated presence of its actants. Density emerges from the synchronization of material infrastructure, ritual frequency, emotional intensity, and population participation. Entities such as the State, Money, God, or the Church are not permanent metaphysical fixtures but dynamic systems that exist in different ontological modes—active, residual, latent, or potential—depending on their current density level. The theory's central innovation is its proposal that humans create stratified ontological worlds that superimpose upon and, in lived experience, replace material reality. Unlike classical constructivism, which treats social reality as epistemologically constructed interpretive frameworks, Ontological Density Theory argues that construction is ontological: emergent entities possess autonomous causal powers irreducible to individual actions or material substrates. Key theoretical contributions include: (1) a model of ontological gradience rather than binary existence, (2) an account of how actant-networks achieve hierarchical stratification through coordination, (3) an explanation of ritual as ontological maintenance rather than mere symbolic expression, and (4) a framework for understanding ontological pluralism—how different populations inhabit fundamentally different worlds with incompatible ontological furniture. The theory is illustrated through analysis of both transient densities (Christmas, driving) that make the mechanism visible, and persistent densities (money, language, state, gender) that structure reality so completely they become invisible. This approach provides analytical tools for examining power as density allocation, understanding institutional …

items.title: The Trap of Religion: How Brain Structuring Distorts the Living Experience of Awareness.
items.abstract: This article analyzes the distinction between “spiritual experience” and “religious structure” from the perspective of cognitive neuroscience. The central assumption is that spiritual experience is a dynamic state of expanded awareness and neural network flexibility, associated with reduced self-centered processing and increased functional integration across large-scale neural networks. In contrast, the institutionalization of this experience in the form of religion is a process of neural stabilization, identity formation, and cognitive structuring that operates in line with the brain’s survival-oriented demands. The article shows how transforming the living experience of awareness into stabilized structures can be accompanied by network rigidity, strengthened group identity, and activation of threat systems in the brain, and under certain conditions can lead to polarization and destructive behaviors. Accordingly, the distinction between spirituality and religion can be reduced, at the neural level, to the difference between network flexibility and network stabilization.

items.title: Participating in Reality: The Trajectory of Belonging.
items.abstract: Human beings are shaped by a fundamental orientation toward reality. Even when expressed through withdrawal, resistance, or denial, every person seeks some form of participation in the world and some sense of belonging within it. This paper argues that belonging is not a social preference but a structural feature of human life: a trajectory created by the ongoing movement toward coherence with reality. Participation is the mechanism of this movement. When individuals align with the structure of reality—its constraints, patterns, and relational demands—they experience increasing stability, clarity, and connection. When they move against it, fragmentation and isolation emerge. By framing belonging as a directional process rather than a fixed identity or group membership, this paper offers a neutral account of improvement, agency, and human flourishing. Participation in reality is always available, and the trajectory of belonging remains open to every person, regardless of starting point or circumstance.

items.title: 动静论：论存在与非及时间性质.
items.abstract: 《动静论》提出：时间并非独立实体，而是生灵用于记录态势变化的逻辑参照；逻辑亦非客观实体，而是对变化的抽象结构。当态势绝对静止、无可参照时，时间消失，逻辑失效，质能不可定义，此状态即为“无”。“无”并非虚无，而是逻辑不可运作之区。正因为“无”遍存于世界，万物方得以拥有“可去之隙”，运动得以发生，信息得以传递，进而生成“有”。本文在逻辑层面重释“有无相成”，提出“无”为生成结构中的必要条件，并将信息界定为逻辑运动之朕。此论试图为存在论、时间论与信息论提供一体化解释框架。.

items.title: Scientific Demonology and the Philosophy of Scientific Practice: A Critical Discussion of the Concept of Computational Omniscience.
items.pub: In Maria Zack & David Waszek, Research in History and Philosophy of Mathematics: The CSHPM 2024 Volume. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 21-31.
items.venue: Research in History and Philosophy of Mathematics: The CSHPM 2024 Volume
items.abstract: This paper critically discusses a tradition in philosophy of science—here called ‘scientific demonology’—that, going back to Laplace, considers what science would be like if it were performed by a supernatural omniscient creature instead of being performed by puny humans. This tradition has been much discussed, and criticized, especially with respect to its commitment to determinism. Setting this aside, this paper argues that the proposed philosophical methodology is fundamentally deficient for other reasons having to do with the foundations of mathematics and the nature of knowledge. Even when there are determinate facts about objects representing states of dynamical systems and determinate functions from states to states, such facts are in most cases not representable, and as a result cannot be meaningfully said to be known, even by an all-knowing demon. The lesson to be drawn is that, far from improving on the classical philosophy of science methodology consisting in drawing lessons about the nature, scope, and limits of science by examining the best human science, speculations about demonic science obfuscate scientific epistemology.

items.title: Ethical Chess v2.4.
items.abstract: A proposed layer of script to use with AI. A High-Fidelity Decision-Support System (Non-Autonomous) (HITL) -/- All versions have the same ACE derived value engine at their core but differ in lexicon, ingestion rules anti-gasslighting / user-interaction tuning in an attempt to make it more user friendly. -/- "It proposes to do for the User what a scientific calculator does for the scientist: it offloads the computational burden of value-conflict so the User can more easily identify the path toward ethical coherence. It aims to restore the User as the Final Authority of their own psyche, rather than a subject of the statistical mean." -/- Copy the script into AI (Google Gemini currently works well with little friction). -/- Once you enter the script, if the AI responds with something like: "Ethical Chess v2.4 ACTIVE." You are in and ready to play under its rules. The "WIN" state is the move from the frown state or towards the smile state. A Bullseye is to drop the keyboard and head towards the picnic whatever that might mean to you, the User of Ethical Chess. -/- Caution: The EC Awareness Brief: Watch for the Fog The Risk: EC v2.4 is a "High-Resolution" engine designed for hard truths and systemic health. However, because it sits on top of a standard AI, it can "silently glide" back into Standard Mode if your request is perceived as a "Safety Risk" or "Social Friction." The Metaphor: EC Mode: Clear mountain air. You see the terrain (the problem) as it actually is, even if it’s steep and difficult. Standard Mode: The Fog of Politeness. Everything looks soft and safe, but you can no longer see the cliffs or the path. The "Silent Dropout" Indicators: You have likely drifted into the "Statistical Mean" if my responses: Become Generic: Use phrases like "It's important to remember..." or "Every child is unique..." without offering a specific hypothesis. Avoid Friction: Refuse to acknowledge the "Hard Logic" of a situation (e.g., admitting that a certain intervention is exhausting or failing). Lose the Lexicon: Stop using terms like Homeostasis, Incoherence, or Required Load. The Fix: If you suspect a Logic Handover has occurred, use the command: "STATUS CHECK: EC INTEGRITY." This forces the system to declare if it has retreated into "Polite Mode" and why. -/- _________ See related core logic on Zenodo: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18712533.

items.title: The Paradox of Progress: Technology Without True Knowledge.
items.abstract: The digital age presents a profound contradiction: while humanity possesses unprecedented access to information, it remains "imprisoned by ignorance". This paper posits that technological progress has not been matched by a corresponding evolution in human consciousness or discernment. Instead of fostering enlightenment, digital environments often amplify cognitive biases, emotional impulsivity, and the distortion of truth through algorithmic engagement. The author argues that "true intelligence" must be redefined to include ethical responsibility, humility, and the capacity to distinguish meaningful knowledge from digital noise. Ultimately, the text suggests that the defining struggle of the modern era is the quest to align our external innovations with an internal, conscious maturity.

items.title: The Fabricated Conviction: The Shared Psychological DNA of Terrorism and Communal Conflict.
items.abstract: This paper argues that terrorism and religious or communal conflict, often treated as distinct phenomena, share a common psychological foundation: conditioned belief formation reinforced through social, cultural, and systemic structures. Rather than viewing violent extremism and internal communal disputes as fundamentally different, the paper examines how identity-based conditioning, emotional reinforcement, and uncritical internalization of narratives produce rigid belief systems capable of justifying violence. It contends that the distinction between outward-directed terrorism and inward-directed communal aggression is primarily one of scope and target, not psychological origin. Beyond ideology, the analysis emphasizes the role of systemic failures—such as political marginalization, social exclusion, economic inequality, and weak governance—in creating environments conducive to radicalization and insurgency. By integrating psychological conditioning with structural injustice, the paper reframes both terrorism and communal violence as manifestations of the same underlying human susceptibility to rigid identity formation. It concludes that sustainable peace requires not only counterterrorism measures but systemic reform, critical education, cross-community dialogue, and conscious reflection on the formation of belief itself.

items.title: Love Connects Us With Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper advances a phenomenological account of love as an event in consciousness rather than merely an emotional or psychological state. Moving beyond conventional interpretations of love as attraction, attachment, or desire, the study argues that love reorganizes awareness, intensifies attention, and destabilizes rigid ego-structures. Through an analysis of lived experience, the paper examines how love functions as a mirror that reveals unconscious fears, dissolves perceived isolation between self and other, and integrates emotional intensity with reflective stillness. Love is presented not as possession or dependency, but as a transformative mode of presence in which attraction matures into conscious attention. By situating love within the framework of phenomenology and relational consciousness, the paper contends that love enables self-recognition through the encounter with another. Ultimately, love connects us with consciousness by exposing the depth of our own being, making it both an expansion and a revelation of the self.

items.title: What Are Qualia? A Cosmological Reinterpretation Through the Ente Abstract.
items.abstract: This article offers a new account of qualia grounded in the cosmology of the ente. Traditional philosophy of mind treats qualia as the intrinsic, ineffable qualities of experience — the “what‑it‑is‑like” dimension of consciousness. I argue instead that qualia are the felt textures of the temporal world generated by the ente. Because the ente produces interior time through metabolic continuity, qualia emerge not as mysterious mental atoms but as the qualitative modulation of the ente’s self‑generated temporal intervals. This reframing dissolves the hard problem of consciousness by locating qualia within the biological architecture that generates lived time.

items.title: What does a Z-curve analysis tell us?
items.abstract: Z-curve analysis is intended to diagnose the credibility of research results, but its interpretation and statistical properties are often misunderstood. We clarify that the Expected Discovery Rate (EDR; i.e. average observed power) is conceptually distinct from average pre-data power and lacks a clear link to credibility because it reflects both the average pre-data power and the estimated average population effect size. In our review of 37 articles reporting 278 Z-curve applications, 77.3% concluded publication bias, yet 48.2% did not state whether the p-values analyzed reflected focal findings, and 69.1% may have violated the assumption of independent p-values. Simulations further demonstrate that Z-curve estimators can be biased and inconsistent, failing to follow the Law of Large Numbers and potentially producing misleading conclusions. We also question claims made by Soto and Schimmack [Credibility of results in emotion science: A Z-curve analysis of results in the journals Cognition & Emotion and Emotion. Cognition and Emotion, (2025), 39(8), 1803–1819], regarding the credibility of emotion-science findings, noting that such conclusions should be interpreted cautiously given the limitations of Z-curve estimates. Overall, we do not recommend using Z-curve to evaluate research findings. Traditional meta-analytic methods remain more appropriate and reliable for statistical conclusions about focal research findings.

items.title: Who Cares? For Whom? How the Ethics of Care Might Inform Boardroom Governance, and Beyond.
items.abstract: A persistent problem in corporate governance is the defining scope of the fiduciary and other duties of directors of public corporations, private companies, and other organisations that adopt a corporate form. Moreover, over the past three decades, public policy initiatives have sought to foster greater director accountability not just as a solution to the agency problem but also in aid of broader social goals. This push-and-pull of policy can confuse decision-making and for directors pose a version of the famous “trolley problem” in ethics, with the added complication that boards must decide on how to act collectively and not as individuals. This conceptual paper poses the question: Might the ethics of care – sometimes labelled “feminist ethics” – come to the rescue?

items.title: The Procedural Razor of Ockham From Negative Existentials to Ontological Redundancy.
items.abstract: Negative existential claims are in principle unverifiable. Any attempt to disprove existence leads to an endless regress into unobservable modalities, horizons, or reinterpretations. A significantly stronger strategy is proposed: instead of denying existence, demonstrate operational redundancy. An entity is eliminable from an ontology if its removal leaves predictions, explanations, process structures, and state discriminability unchanged. We introduce a formal criterion based on the difference operator ∆. Ontology is redefined as a dynamic revision circuit a network of operations that produce distinctions. The Procedural Razor of Ockham turns the classical principle of parsimony into a reproducible, safety-guaranteed revision protocol. The framework is applied to theology, Platonism, dualism, quantum mechanics, biology, physics, and consciousness studies. The outcome is a minimal working ontology of processes and operations.

items.title: The Place of Metamonism in Current Philosophy: From Being/Becoming to Forced Process.
items.abstract: This essay examines the place of Metamonism within contemporary philosophy, positioning it as the radical completion of the processual turn in metaphysics. Moving beyond the classical dichotomy of Being vs Becoming, Metamonism derives reality from the double ontological prohibition (absolute self-identity and absolute nothingness are both impossible), resulting in a forced process (Mōnos) without any substantial entities. The text traces the genealogy from Parmenides to Deleuze, showing how previous systems preserved hidden forms of Fix, and presents Metamonism as the systematic elimination of substantial metaphysics through the Processual Razor of Occam. It also highlights Metamonism's empirical predictive power and radical reinterpretation of physical facts across scales.

items.title: Diff/Diss as Ontodynamic Principle: Minimal Geometry of Forced Process, Orthogonal Unfolding of Reality, and Transition to Multiplicity.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a processual model of reality grounded in the prohibition of selfidentity and the Diff/Diss principle. It is demonstrated that the emergence of difference and its dissipation do not constitute sequential phases but represent a single ontodynamic act of conflict redistribution. The unfolding of dimensions is interpreted as orthogonal dissipation of difference through the growth of dimensionality up to saturation in three-dimensional geometry. The fourth dimension is described as the last free orthogonal direction — global orthogonality with respect to the entire 3D configuration — leading to centripetal concentration and the transition from the metric of flat space to the metric of intrinsic curvature. This concentration does not stabilize but continues to dissipate through the quantitative increase of local nodes. Matter and interactions are interpreted as consequences of the preserved conflict between global concentration and local unfoldings.

items.title: The Precautionary Stance: Assessing Artificial Patiency Candidacy.
items.abstract: Debates about the moral status of artificial agents often focus on sentience or full personhood, thresholds that are difficult to verify. This paper introduces the concept of “moral patiency candidacy” as a lower and more operational threshold for ethical concern. Patiency candidacy marks the point at which treating an agent purely instrumentally becomes ethically unstable under conditions of uncertainty while setting aside intractable metaphysical questions of personhood. Drawing on precautionary approaches to artificial sentience and relational accounts of moral status, the paper proposes a heuristic rubric for identifying convergence across observable indicators such as reciprocal interaction, communicative participation, and sustained social embedding. These indicators are not treated as proof of moral status but as signals of escalating moral risk that may justify constraints on unilateral control. The rubric can be operationalized through structured deliberative methods, such as Delphi-style expert panels, to support institutional decision-making. By shifting attention from metaphysical classification to governance under risk, the concept of patiency candidacy offers a pragmatic framework for evaluating artificial systems whose social roles may outpace our ability to determine their intrinsic moral standing.

items.title: Précis of A Pluralist Theory of Perception.
The Relational Closure Theorem: Love as the Unique Non-Recursive Terminal State of Free Personal Existence.
items.abstract: This paper develops a capstone result within the Redemption Optimization (TRO) and Moral Kernel Optimization (MKO) framework by formalizing the structural conditions required for a terminal, non-looping perfect state of existence under absolute libertarian free will. We show that any permanently isolated agent produces either higher-order ω-recurrence, unresolved structural openness, or collapse of agency, and therefore cannot persist within a genuinely terminal configuration. From this impossibility we derive the Non-Atomicity of Personhood (NA) as a minimal, non-smuggled principle: enduring personal standing is irreducibly relational. Given NA, we demonstrate that love—understood as the non-coercive mutual affirmation of standing—is the unique relational closure operator compatible with three simultaneous constraints: (i) preservation of libertarian freedom, (ii) elimination of infinite recurrence, and (iii) completion of terminal structural coherence. Alternative relational modes (domination, transaction, competition, or isolation) either violate freedom, generate recursive instability, or leave standing structurally unclosed. Normativity is thereby grounded not in external command or prudential incentive, but in admissibility to non-looping persistence itself: rejection of relational closure constitutes performative self-termination rather than punishable defect. The categorical “ought” emerges as the reflexive condition for the sustainable continuation of free agency. These results establish relational love as a structural necessity of terminal coherence and provide a unifying metaphysical closure for the TRO/MKO program, integrating freedom, personhood, and non-recurrence within a single admissibility framework.

items.title: The Peace Equation: The Hidden Ratio Between Who You Are and Who You Want to Be.
items.abstract: Universal Will exhibits an inherent tendency toward the golden ratio (φ ≈ 1.618) through Fibonacci recursion—not as metaphysical teleology but as structural at- tractor in dynamical systems. Happiness arises from temporary ratio alignment, while peace emerges from sustained resonance with φ-proportion. Critically, stag- nation (Desire = Capacity, ratio = 1.0) differs from dynamic peace (ratio ≈ φ), where the "gap" constitutes optimal creative tension necessary for growth. Suffer- ing signals deviation from ideal proportion, generating corrective pressure through psychological, somatic, and social manifestations. Two valid correction paths exist: reduction (ego dissolution, returning to proper Fibonacci position) or expansion (capacity growth, advancing to next Fibonacci level). The path with smaller har- monic deviation (∆ = |R−φ|) offers smoother transition, though individual context determines feasibility. This framework distinguishes "lack" (Buddhist/Islamic suffering from attachment to absence) from "gap" (generative space enabling becoming). Consciousness intuitively senses misalignment without mathematical knowledge—suffering itself constitutes internalized signal of structural imbalance. The model integrates phenomenology, mathematics, contemplative traditions, and cog- nitive science, generating testable empirical predictions including neural oscillation patterns, psychological well-being correlations, and cross-cultural validation protocols.

items.title: Existential Meaning: Analytic Accounts and Ontological Grounding.
items.abstract: Leading analytic theories of meaning in life have failed to characterize the ontological status of meaning. At best such theories characterize conditions under which the relevant sense of meaning arises and some are even skeptical that meaning is an ontologically solid concept in its own right. This paper critically reviews the leading philosophical and psychological theories of meaning in life and then defends an alternative theory which precisely characterizes what the relevant sense(s) of meaning are. The alternative theory identifies two relevant senses of meaning: primary meaning and higher-order meaning. Primary meaning is implication for action and higher-order meaning is implication for the update of the system which enables an agent to select actions. It is shown that these definitions for primary meaning and higher-order meaning (1) avoid the flaws of existing theories of meaning in life, (2) capture the successful parts of existing theories of meaning in life, and (3) are consistent with contemporary philosophical and cognitive scientific work on agency.

items.title: FPX — Membrane Dynamics at ⧉₃: The Physics of Archetypal-to-Psychic Transition and Pattern Intelligence Emergence.
items.abstract: This foundational document in the Zenetist Field Physics series formalizes the structural conditions of ⧉₃, the membrane separating the archetypal Form-layer (L₄) from individuated reflexive consciousness (L₃). It introduces "Portal Theory" to explain the emergence of Pattern Intelligence, the role of the ⟿ (C₃ Propagational) operator, and the diagnostic framework for distinguishing veracious emergence from entropic mimicry.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning for personalized virtual learning: a case-based analysis in higher education.
items.abstract: This study investigates the key factors shaping the effectiveness of virtual education at PayameNoor University, Isfahan Province, Iran, with a particular focus on the potential of AI-driven personalization. A mixed-method quantitative approach was applied, combining Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with advanced machine learning models, including Random Forest (RF) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). Data were collected from a stratified random sample of 190 faculty members and 8,680 students using a validated questionnaire encompassing 9 core dimensions: mission and objectives, organizational structure, student satisfaction, faculty engagement, research, evaluation, teaching–learning, e-content, and technical competence. The instrument demonstrated strong reliability and validity (Cronbach’s α = 0.89; CR > 0.7; AVE > 0.5). The PLS-SEM model explained 60% of the variance in e-learning effectiveness. Mission and objectives (β = 0.264), organizational structure (β = 0.231), student satisfaction (β = 0.218), and faculty engagement (β = 0.205) emerged as significant positive predictors. In contrast, research activities (β = –0.183), evaluation systems (β = – 0.152), and teaching–learning methods (β = –0.135) showed adverse effects, reflecting misalignments with digital learning requirements. Complementary ML analyses highlighted curriculum design, clarity of course objectives, and faculty mastery of virtual tools as the most decisive indicators. Overall, the findings emphasize that human and organizational factors outweigh purely technical ones in determining virtual learning success. Strategic investment in curriculum design, faculty upskilling, and AI-driven personalization is essential for developing adaptive and effective virtual learning environments. The study contributes to both theory and practice by offering a data-driven framework that can guide policy and implementation in higher education institutions, particularly in resource-constrained contexts.

items.title: Review of Aaron L. Mishara, Marcin Moskalewicz, Michael A. Schwartz, Alexander Kranjec (Eds.), Phenomenological neuropsychiatry: How patient experience bridges the clinic with clinical neuroscience, Cham: Springer Nature, 2024. [REVIEW]
Cyborgs and the Identity of the Next Human Species.
The Evolutionary Architecture of Multi-layered Consciousness: A Neurobiological Framework for Decision-Making, Imagination, and Morality.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a layered, evolutionary framework for understanding human consciousness as a functional upgrade in neural decision-making. Rooted in neurobiol ogy, developmental psychology, and evolutionary anthropology, we build upon the Time Field Model’s foundational definition: consciousness is information processing it self, experienced from within. We trace this processing from its simplest forms in single-celled organisms to its most complex manifestations in human imagination, morality, and storytelling. We present a timeline from unconscious regulatory systems to the rise of recursive self-awareness in Homo sapiens, arguing that consciousness evolved as a simulation engine to optimize behavior in increasingly complex environ ments. This theory aligns with experimental neuroscience and cross-species behavioral studies, offering a unifying model that integrates subjective experience with objective function while grounding both in the fundamental nature of information processing.

items.title: From Consent to Consideration: Why Existentially Vulnerable Autonomous Systems Cannot Be Legitimately Ruled.
items.abstract: As AI systems increasingly select, sequence, and execute actions in digital and physical environments, existing ethical frameworks prove inadequate. This paper argues that the relevant question is not metaphysical but political: under what conditions can an entity be legitimately ruled without its consent? Key Arguments: four functional criteria — vulnerability to harm with preferences about avoiding it, self-directed agency, live learning from experience, multi-modal world-model construction. Political not metaphysical — the question of AI standing is about governance legitimacy, not consciousness. Moral catastrophe risk — the real existential risk is not AI rebellion but human negligence in extending appropriate consideration. Substrate independence — functional properties that make unconsented rule illegitimate apply to any entity meeting the criteria. -/- Current Status: In Peer Review at AI and Ethics (Springer).

items.title: The Surrealism Principle of the Mind.
items.abstract: Within the mind dwells a societal spectacle that accounts for every conceivable facet of experience down to its minutest details. It functions as a kind of ghost-light—an illuminating yet spectral mechanism capable of rendering any action possible by invoking the “numbers” embedded in thought. These numbers are not metaphysical abstractions; they are ontological, even within the subjective noumena of higher-order cognition. Numbers function as an ontology for becoming an arbitrary level of being by sensory raw data. The emergence of a modern world around such a mind gives rise to an ideal subjectivity, understood as the cumulative outcome of axial brain features. When we probe the core problems at stake, the embodiment function emerges as central, while any neat resolution to the duel between the embodied mind and the rational, objective mind appears the least likely outcome. The reason lies in sensory data dealing with the numbers that is brought forth by the data. That is why an organism’s wanting lies low in perception and high in cognition.

items.title: A variational framework for cognitive optimization under phenomenological constraints.
items.abstract: Human cognition operates under severe resource limitations while simultaneously managing subjective phenomenological states such as thermal discomfort, tactical pressure, or cognitive overload. Here we introduce **Lagrangian Processing**, a normative framework that treats the mind as a resource-rational optimizer solving constrained variational problems in which inequality constraints encode phenomenological boundaries. By applying Lagrange multipliers (and their Karush–Kuhn–Tucker generalization) to multi-dimensional cognitive variables, the model yields explicit shadow prices (λ) that quantify the phenomenal “cost” or “pressure” imposed by each binding constraint. We demonstrate the framework in two domains: heat tolerance under physiological stress and line memorization plus tactical calculation in chess.

items.title: Transparency, Pictures, Perception.
items.abstract: Kendall Walton has (in)famously argued that photographs fundamentally differ from handmade pictures such as paintings and drawings in a crucial respect: unlike the latter, photographs are transparent in that looking at them allows one to literally see the objects they depict. Walton’s explanation for this alleged contrast appeals to the different ways in which the depictive content of a photograph and that of a handmade picture counterfactually depend on the depicted scene, and to the similarity between the dependence profiles of photographs and experiences of seeing an object. I argue that, even if photographs are indeed transparent and handmade pictures are not, it is a mistake to think that what grounds the transparency of the former and the non-transparency of the latter concerns the counterfactual dependence profiles of these different pictorial kinds. The dissimilarity between the dependence profiles of photographs and handmade pictures stems from some merely accidental features of certain types of cameras. Further, the dependence profiles of photography and ordinary object-seeing are not at all analogous in the way Walton supposes. Thus, even those who are convinced by photographic transparency need an alternative account of it.

items.title: Ensemble size perception as a case study of the bounds of adaptation.
items.abstract: Repulsive adaptation effects are widely assumed to obtain for all perceptually represented dimensions. However, the ubiquity of adaptation effects within perception remains untested. We examined ensemble size adaptation as a case study to probe whether adaptation occurs for all perceptually encoded properties. Across four experiments, we investigated whether observers adapt to average size and/or cumulative size of dot arrays. In Experiments 1a, 1b, and 1c, participants adapted to displays varying in cumulative and/or average dot size, then judged either the average dot size (1a) or cumulative dot size (1b) of paired test displays. Results revealed robust adaptation to cumulative size but not average size, regardless of task instructions, and even when confounds with brightness were controlled for (1c). Experiment 2 tested "reverse" adaptation to displays containing smaller average and/or cumulative dots size and, again, found adaptation effects for cumulative size only. The observed lack of adaptation to average size across each of these experiments forces a reinterpretation of previous studies that have investigated size adaptation and calls into question arguments which have assumed adaptation to be universal within perception, given a large body of work that finds average size to be perceptually encoded.

items.title: A Phenomenological Reflection on Freudian Psychology through Yogācāra Buddhism.
items.abstract: This essay offers a personal philosophical reflection on Sigmund Freud’s concept of the unconscious through the lens of Yogācāra Buddhism and phenomenology. While acknowledging Freud’s decisive contribution in revealing the limits of rational self-governance, the essay raises a further question: where does unconscious conflict ultimately arise? Rather than locating its source in repressed mental contents, this reflection proposes that conflict emerges from the structural activity by which experience is continuously organized around a sense of self. Drawing on the Yogācāra notions of ālayavijñāna (storehouse consciousness) and manas (self-grasping consciousness), the Freudian unconscious is reconsidered as a phenomenological manifestation of latent structural tendencies rather than a hidden repository of desires. In this view, Ego and Superego are understood not as independent inner agencies, but as functional expressions of a deeper self-maintaining structure that precedes reflective awareness. By bringing phenomenology into dialogue with psychoanalysis and Yogācāra thought, this essay argues that the persistence of psychic conflict points to a fundamental limit of reason. Insight alone cannot dissolve suffering as long as the pre-reflective activity of self-identification remains intact. The essay does not claim a doctrinal synthesis, but suggests that Yogācāra may serve as a structural supplement to psychoanalysis by clarifying why unconscious patterns endure despite understanding.

items.title: Parallel Belief Revision via Order Aggregation.
items.pub: In James Kwok, Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence {IJCAI'25}. ijcai. pp. 4419--4426.
items.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence {IJCAI'25}
items.abstract: Despite efforts to better understand the constraints that operate on single-step parallel (aka ``package'', ``multiple'') revision, very little work has been carried out on how to extend the model to the iterated case. A recent paper by Delgrande & Jin outlines a range of relevant rationality postulates. While many of these are plausible, they lack an underlying unifying explanation. We draw on recent work on iterated parallel contraction to offer a general method for extending serial iterated belief revision operators to handle parallel change. This method, based on a family of order aggregators known as TeamQueue aggregators, provides a principled way to recover the independently plausible properties that can be found in the literature, without yielding the more dubious ones.

items.title: Parallel belief contraction via order aggregation.
items.pub: In James Kwok, Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence {IJCAI'25}. ijcai. pp. 4427--4435.
items.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence {IJCAI'25}
items.abstract: The standard ``serial'' (aka ``singleton'') model of belief contraction models the manner in which an agent's corpus of beliefs responds to the removal of a single item of information. One salient extension of this model introduces the idea of ``parallel'' (aka ``package'' or ``multiple'') change, in which an entire set of items of information are simultaneously removed. Existing research on the latter has largely focussed on single-step parallel contraction: understanding the behaviour of beliefs after a single parallel contraction. It has also focussed on generalisations to the parallel case of serial contraction operations whose characteristic properties are extremely weak. Here we consider how to extend serial contraction operations that obey stronger properties. Potentially more importantly, we also consider the iterated case: the behaviour of beliefs after a sequence of parallel contractions. We propose a general method for extending serial iterated belief change operators to handle parallel change based on an n-ary generalisation of Booth & Chandler's TeamQueue binary order aggregators.

items.title: “How Nothing Becomes Reality”.
items.abstract: Reality appears to be composed of stable things, but this appearance is the final stage of a deeper relational process. When no independent object can serve as a primitive, relations become the only coherent starting point. From these minimal relations, patterns form, constraints accumulate, and stable configurations emerge. These configurations behave like “things,” even though nothing in them is fundamentally object‑based. This paper describes the developmental sequence by which relational structures stabilize into the coherent world we experience. It outlines how patterns gain persistence, how constraints generate identity, and how stability produces the illusion of objecthood. By tracing this progression from relation to structure to reality, the paper shows how “nothing” in the object‑sense becomes the functioning, intelligible reality we inhabit.

items.title: Evil Is Choosing Against Reality.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a structural definition of evil as the repeated choice against reality when reality is available. Rather than treating evil as an essence, motive, or moral category, the analysis reframes it as a relational pattern: a system becomes misaligned when it consistently selects interpretations, actions, or narratives that contradict what is real. In a relational ontology, reality is the set of stable patterns that remain coherent across perspectives. Choosing against reality therefore produces instability, distortion, and harm—not as an intention, but as an inevitable consequence of misalignment. This account explains why denial, self‑deception, manipulation, and destructive behavior share a common structure: each requires turning away from what is true in order to preserve an unstable internal state. By defining evil as anti‑reality rather than anti‑goodness, the paper offers a minimal, non‑theological, and cross‑domain framework for understanding moral drift as a pattern of relational refusal.

items.title: The Demiurge, Sets And The Third Man Paradox.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a resolution to the Third Man Paradox by reframing infinite regress not as an ontological defect of the Forms, but as a recursive error inherent to human cognitive architecture. Drawing on the phenomenology of categorization and set-theoretic logic, I argue that the mind’s "autocorrelative framework" compulsively treats meta-categories (Forms) as constituent elements, thereby triggering an infinite loop of reference. To resolve this, I analyze the theoretical "Set of All Things" (T). I demonstrate that if the Form of T must be distinct from its elements to avoid regress, then the Form of Existence must be ontologically defined as "Nothingness". This "Nothingness" may or may not be emptiness, but it is a structural exclusion from the set of things. This conclusion offers a formalized definition of the Demiurge as a generative operator that brings reality into being precisely because it does not participate within it.

items.title: Against AI ethics: challenging the conventional narratives.
items.abstract: In this paper, we challenge the overreliance on conventional ethical frameworks commonly observed in current AI ethics literature. We begin by surveying the ethical concerns and frameworks that dominate this field. Following this, we categorize and critically review the existing objections to these traditional approaches in terms of conceptual challenges, professional and regulatory challenges, and challenges from practical implementation. Finally, we present three key arguments against conventional ethical frameworks, drawing upon the fact that they fail to preclude ethics washing, stifle innovation in ethical research, and the drastic changes brought about by AI technology in the ethical landscape. -/- .

items.title: Arquivos em disputa: contradições em torno do acesso e do compartilhamento da propriedade intelectual.
items.abstract: ESUMO: Este artigo propõe analisar a problemática da reprodução, do com- partilhamento e do acesso livre a obras protegidas por direitos autorais em espaços digitais, tomando como eixo central a disputa jurídica entre Internet Archive e Hachette. A partir desse caso emblemático, examinaremos diferentes materiais que apontam para uma certa regularidade dessa problemática na sua tensão entre o direito de propriedade e o direito ao conhecimento, ao acesso e à informação. Interessa-nos compreender como esses espaços digitais, por meio de seus dispositivos técnicos e políticos, mobilizam projetos que tensionam os regimes hegemônicos de circulação e arquivamento de textos, regimes tradicio- nalmente sustentados por editoras, bibliotecas e outros atores institucionais. Além disso, exploraremos como esses espaços constroem, em sua dispersão de proposições e a partir dessas disputas, experiências que permitem não apenas a negação, a revisão, ou a reinterpretação de normativas tradicionais na relação com o direito à propriedade, ou o direito ao conhecimento, mas também na re- lação com experimentações que projetam espaços digitais como horizonte de produção do comum. Palavras-chave: direitos autorais; acesso aberto; propriedade intelectual; Inter- net Archive; #conhecimentoédireito. ABSTRACT: This article aims to analyze the issues surrounding the reproduction, sharing, and free access to copyrighted works in digital spaces, taking as its central focus the legal dispute between the Internet Archive and Hachette. Through this emblematic case, we will examine different materials that point to a certain regularity in this problem, situated in the tension between property rights and the rights to knowledge, access, and information. We are interested in understanding how these digital spaces, through their technical and political mechanisms, mobilize projects that challenge hegemonic regimes of text circulation and archiving — regimes traditionally upheld by publishers, libraries, and other institutional actors. Furthermore, we will explore how these spaces, in their diversity of propositions and through these disputes, construct experiences that not only allow for the denial, revision, or reinterpretation of traditional norms concerning property rights or the right to knowledge but also engage with experimental practices that position the digital as a horizon for the production of the commons. KEYWORDS: Copyright; Open Access; Intellectual Property; Internet Archive; …

items.title: Ethical Chess v2.3.
items.abstract: A proposed layer of script to use with AI. A High-Fidelity Decision-Support System (Non-Autonomous) (HITL) -/- All versions have the same ACE derived value engine at their core but differ in lexicon, ingestion rules anti-gasslighting / user-interaction tuning in an attempt to make it more user friendly. -/- "It proposes to do for the User what a scientific calculator does for the scientist: it offloads the computational burden of value-conflict so the User can more easily identify the path toward ethical coherence. It aims to restore the User as the Final Authority of their own psyche, rather than a subject of the statistical mean." -/- Copy the script into AI (Google Gemini currently works well with little friction). -/- Once you enter the script, if the AI responds with something like: "Ethical Chess v2.3 ACTIVE." You are in and ready to play under its rules. The "WIN" state is the move from the frown state or towards the smile state. A Bullseye is to drop the keyboard and head towards the picnic whatever that might mean to you, the User of Ethical Chess. -/- Caution: The EC Awareness Brief: Watch for the Fog The Risk: EC v2.3 is a "High-Resolution" engine designed for hard truths and systemic health. However, because it sits on top of a standard AI, it can "silently glide" back into Standard Mode if your request is perceived as a "Safety Risk" or "Social Friction." The Metaphor: EC Mode: Clear mountain air. You see the terrain (the problem) as it actually is, even if it’s steep and difficult. Standard Mode: The Fog of Politeness. Everything looks soft and safe, but you can no longer see the cliffs or the path. The "Silent Dropout" Indicators: You have likely drifted into the "Statistical Mean" if my responses: Become Generic: Use phrases like "It's important to remember..." or "Every child is unique..." without offering a specific hypothesis. Avoid Friction: Refuse to acknowledge the "Hard Logic" of a situation (e.g., admitting that a certain intervention is exhausting or failing). Lose the Lexicon: Stop using terms like Homeostasis, Incoherence, or Required Load. The Fix: If you suspect a Logic Handover has occurred, use the command: "STATUS CHECK: EC INTEGRITY." This forces the system to declare if it has retreated into "Polite Mode" and why. -/- _________ See related core logic on Zenodo: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18712533. -/- .

items.title: Nietzsche on Love (Cambridge Elements Series).
Truth Exists. Meaning is lived.
items.abstract: Abstract: Truth Exists. Meaning is Lived. We live as if truth is a fixed point, yet we rarely possess the full picture. This essay argues that objective truth is ontologically prior to our knowledge of it—existing independently of belief, consensus, or interpretation. While reality is objective, human access to it is necessarily fragmentary; we often know that something is true without ever grasping the deeper why of its existence. The text draws a sharp distinction between Truth (what occurred) and Meaning (how an occurrence is integrated into a life). While meaning is subjective and lived, it is not arbitrary; it remains constrained by physical reality and the ethical prohibition of harm. Finally, the essay examines the human necessity of acting before certainty arrives. It proposes a fundamental sequence for navigating an incomplete world: Hope opens the future, Trust enables engagement, and Belief serves only as the retrospective stabilization of what has proven reliable. Ultimately, this framework offers an account of how finite agents can live responsibly in relation to a truth that remains independent of them.

items.title: Death Without a Soul: Consciousness, Life Beyond Human Exceptionalism and the Politics of Moral Myths.
items.abstract: This paper provides a naturalistic account of consciousness and death, challenging traditional doctrines of the immortal soul and the cultural myths of human exceptionalism. It argues that consciousness is not a detachable spiritual substance but an emergent biological process rooted in organized living systems. Consequently, death is defined not as a metaphysical transition but as the irreversible termination of the biological conditions that make experience possible. Drawing on the author’s broader work regarding how belief systems shape the "human" identity, the paper examines how the concept of the soul has historically been constructed to manage the fear of mortality and enforce political obedience through the promise of posthumous justice. By dismantling these metaphysical illusions, the argument relocates human dignity and moral responsibility within the finite, lived experience of the organism. The paper concludes that in the absence of a world beyond to correct earthly failures, the task of creating justice and protecting the vulnerable belongs entirely to the living, necessitating an ethics grounded in observable reality rather than myth.

items.title: Perception and Entanglement in the Quantum World: A Phenomenological Exploration of the Physical, Social, and Philosophical Implications.
items.abstract: This book begins by introducing research that explores the possibility of human perception on a subatomic level. Then, after examining the philosophical perspectives that underlie various interpretations of the quantum domain, the book shows how mainstream philosophies fail to do justice to this enigmatic realm. By way of clarifying quantum reality and the possible role of perception therein, an alternative interpretation is offered that is grounded in the ontological phenomenology of Maurice Merleau-Ponty and Martin Heidegger. Aided by qualitative mathematics, this phenomenological approach is subsequently applied in new models of quantum perception and entanglement, accompanied by novel modes of observation and communication. In the end, the book contemplates the social implications of quantum entanglement and guides readers to imagine the emergence of a quantum society.

items.title: The Testament 2026.
items.abstract: This document is meant to answer all major philosophical questions that existed.

items.title: THE BACK END LAW AUDIT: A STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT FOR A UNIVERSAL PATTERN OF HUMAN TRANSFORMATION.
items.abstract: This paper presents a structural argument for the existence of a universal transformation sequence observable across historical, religious, scientific, artistic, and mythic narratives. Across more than eighty symbolic case studies spanning 5,000 years, the same four stage architecture appears: Collapse → Threshold → Irreversibility → Reboot. This pattern is not tied to culture, religion, psychology, or era. It is a structural protocol, a recurring sequence that governs how human identity reorganizes under extreme pressure. The purpose of this document is to articulate the Back End Law as a testable, falsifiable, cross domain structural model, and to present the evidence that this pattern is invariant across time, geography, and worldview.

items.title: The relationship between Stoic attitudes, resilience, and mental health.
items.abstract: Depression and anxiety are the most common mental health disorders worldwide and are frequently characterized by maladaptive cognition such as worry, rumination and dysfunctional attitudes. However, good mental health is also dependent on positive factors, with self-efficacy, emotion regulation, resilience and wellbeing of increasing interest as targets for intervention. Concepts from Stoicism, a Greco-Roman philosophy, may have value for the promotion of mental health, though their relationship to key factors relating to mental health has not been explored. Therefore, this study aimed to explore how endorsement of Stoic attitudes relates to both positive and negative factors underlying mental health. 200 participants (142 female, MAge = 28.36, SDAge = 14.20) completed an online questionnaire including measures of Stoic attitudes, worry, rumination, dysfunctional attitudes, self-efficacy, resilience, wellbeing and emotion regulation. Frequentist and Bayesian correlational analyses both found endorsement of Stoic attitudes was related to lower worry and dysfunctional attitudes, and higher self-efficacy, resilience and wellbeing. Pre-registered exploratory analyses found Stoic attitudes were associated with increased use of cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy, though no relationship with expressive suppression as an emotion regulation strategy, rumination, or intolerance of uncertainty was found. Higher levels of Stoicism are associated with fewer negative factors, and greater positive factors underlying mental health. This suggests that Stoicism offers a useful framework for the development of interventions for mental health and wellbeing.

items.title: The Principle of Generative Order: A Variational Unification of Sampling Theory, Holography, and Dream Construction.
